seoTitle: Pet Groomer Email, SMS & Loyalty Marketing Guide
description: Email and SMS marketing for pet groomers: templates, reminders, newsletters and tools like Mailchimp and Klaviyo to keep clients rebooking on time.
intro: This guide covers email and SMS marketing for pet groomers. It includes beginner overviews, ready-to-adapt templates, newsletters, appointment reminders and tool walkthroughs for Mailchimp and Klaviyo. It is for groomers who want regular clients to rebook on schedule instead of drifting away.

With little budget, start by collecting client emails and phone numbers at checkout, with permission. Then set up one simple rebooking reminder and a short monthly note using a free or low-cost plan. Read the beginner guide and templates first, and add a newsletter once reminders are working.

Reminders and templates are easy to run on your own. A more elaborate setup, such as segmented lists or loyalty offers, takes more care, and you need to follow consent and unsubscribe rules. If you would like help building it, DataLatte can support you, but a simple reminder system covers most of the value.

faq.q: Is email or SMS better for pet groomers?
faq.a: Each has a place. SMS suits appointment reminders because messages are seen quickly, while email works for newsletters and longer updates. Many groomers use both, with permission.

faq.q: What should I put in a pet grooming email?
faq.a: Keep it simple: a friendly greeting, a rebooking reminder or seasonal tip, a clear booking link and your contact details. One main action per email works best.

faq.q: Do I need permission to text or email clients?
faq.a: Yes. Rules differ by country, so get clear consent, include opt-out options and check your local regulations. When unsure, ask a professional.

faq.q: Which email tool should a groomer use?
faq.a: Mailchimp and Klaviyo are common options, and pricing and features change, so compare current plans. Pick the simplest tool you will actually use.
